research_object: Task-level emergent capability of human-only, AI-only, and hybrid groups under matched budgets
hypotheses: Functional diversity and complementary errors can create group advantage over the best member.
Independent first judgments can protect aggregation from social herding.
Calibrated human-AI role complementarity can outperform authority-centered assistance.
Communication and coordination have task- and topology-dependent optima.
Held-out cross-task transfer is required for a strong emergence claim.
Mechanism metrics explain group advantage better than group size alone.
hard_boundary: DESIGN_ONLY; no group mind, consciousness, social ranking, or fabricated empirical finding is claimed.
